title: Normal projective compactification over a complete trait
statement: A trait means the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring, a Noetherian local domain of dimension one with principal maximal ideal. A complete strictly henselian trait has a maximal-ideal-adically complete henselian coordinate ring with separably closed residue field. Mixed characteristic means fraction-field characteristic zero and positive residue characteristic. Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a complete strictly henselian mixed-characteristic trait, with fraction field $K$, and let $X$ be an integral regular scheme flat and quasi-projective of finite type over $S$. There exist a finite dominant extension of complete strictly henselian traits $S_0\to S$, a normal integral projective $S_0$-scheme $C$, and a dense open immersion $X\hookrightarrow C$ over $S$. The structural morphism $C\to S_0$ is flat and its generic fibre is geometrically integral (its base change to every field extension of $k(S_0)$ is integral). For an integral scheme $W$ with generic point $\xi$ [def-sc-generic-point], its function field is the stalk $k(W)=\mathcal O_{W,\xi}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. The embedding identifies $k(C)=k(X)$, and $k(S_0)$ is the algebraic closure of $K$ in this function field. No base change of $X$ and no extension of its function field is part of the conclusion. Integral, regular, flat, finite type, finite, projective, and etale use [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-kun-projective], and [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Normal means all local rings are integrally closed domains. Quasi-projective means admitting a locally closed immersion into some finite-dimensional projective space over the base. Smoothness is as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and geometric integrality, reducedness, connectedness and irreducibility as in [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible].

proof.text: Write $F=k(X)$. Let $\xi$ be the generic point of the nonempty integral scheme $X$ and $s$ its image in $S$. Flatness at $\xi$ [def-weil-flat-morphism] says that $F=\mathcal O_{X,\xi}$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{S,s}$, which is $R$ (if $s$ is the closed point) or $K$ (if $s$ is the generic point). In the first case [lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain] shows that nonzero elements of $R$ act injectively on the nonzero field $F$; in the second case they act through units of $K$. In both cases nonzero elements of $R$ act injectively on $F$. Thus $R\hookrightarrow F$ and $K\hookrightarrow F$. On a nonempty affine finite-type chart of $X$, the generic prime contracts to $(0)\subset R$, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-residue-field-extension-finitely-generated] gives that $F/K$ is finitely generated. Let $L$ be the subfield of elements of $F$ algebraic over $K$. By [lem-zl-finite-algebraic-closure], $L/K$ is finite. Mixed characteristic gives characteristic zero, so [lem-weil-pbc-char-zero-field-extension-separable] makes this finite extension separable.

source.place: ILO XVI 3.7, first paragraph, printed p.254: preparation of the algebraic constants; Fields Tag 037J; Algebra Tag 00TX; residue-field finite generation as recorded in the cited node.

proof.text: Choose the locally closed immersion $X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_S$ in the quasi-projectivity hypothesis. It is quasi-compact: $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], hence each open subset of $X$ is quasi-compact. Projective space is separated over the affine $S$ by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper] and the definition of properness. Apply [sk-lem-nagata-sketch-closure] to form its scheme-theoretic image $Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_S$. It gives an open immersion $X\hookrightarrow Y$ which is schematically dense. The underlying space of $Y$ is the closure of the irreducible $X$, hence irreducible. For any nonempty affine open $V\subset Y$, schematic density injects $\mathcal O_Y(V)$ into $\mathcal O_X(V\cap X)$, which embeds in $F$; thus this ring is a domain. Therefore $Y$ is integral, $X$ is dense in it, and $k(Y)=F$. Its displayed closed immersion makes $Y\to S$ projective.

source.place: Tag 01WA, lemma-H-quasi-projective-open-H-projective, proof via scheme-theoretic closure; finite type over Noetherian Tag 01T6.

proof.text:
The complete Noetherian local ring $R$ is excellent by [lem-per-complete-local-excellence]. On each standard affine projective chart the ring of $Y$ is a quotient of $R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, so $Y$ is finite type over $S$ and is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. These chart rings are finite-type $R$-algebras and are excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]. Since $Y$ is covered by these affine opens, [lem-trf-excellent-scheme-affine-cover] makes the coordinate ring of every affine open of $Y$ excellent, which is the excellence hypothesis of the preparation node. Form the normalization $
u:C=Y^
u	o Y$ in $F$ using [def-sc-normalization]. Since $Y$ is reduced, excellent and Noetherian, [lem-per-excellent-normalization-preparation] gives that $
u$ is finite and surjective and $C$ is normal and Noetherian. The componentwise normalization has one component here: on any nonempty affine chart its ring is the integral closure of a domain in $F$, hence a domain. Thus $C$ is integral and $k(C)=F$.

source.place: Tags 035S, lemma-nagata-normalization; 035Q, lemma-normalization-normal; More on Algebra Tags 07QW and 07QU.

proof.text: Regularity of $X$ implies normality by [rem-pc-regular-normal]. We check the normalization over the entire original open, not just over an unspecified dense open. If $A=\mathcal O_X(U)$ for a nonempty affine open $U\subset X$, an element of $F$ integral over $A$ is integral over every local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ for $x\in U$; normality places it in every such local ring. By [lem-sc-function-field-sections-glue] it belongs to $A$, so $A$ is integrally closed in $F$. On a chart of $Y$ the normalization is integral closure in $F$; [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization] identifies its restriction to each principal open with the integral closure of that open. Principal opens of charts of $Y$ contained in $X$ cover $X$. The preceding equality therefore shows $\nu^{-1}X\cong X$ over $Y$. Its inverse gives a dense open immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow C$, and the induced function-field identification is $k(C)=k(X)=F$.

source.place: Tag 0307, algebra-lemma-integral-closure-localize, applied to normalization charts; Tag 035Q; normality of regular schemes Tag 0569.

proof.text: The projective embedding $Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_S$, with affine $S$, supplies an ample invertible sheaf on $Y$ by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-ample-invertible]. The finite map $\nu:C\to Y$ is projective in the projective-bundle convention by [lem-trf-finite-projective-bundle]. Because $Y$ has the stated ample sheaf, [lem-trf-projective-bundle-to-h-projective] upgrades this to the finite-projective-space convention. Apply [lem-trf-h-projective-composition] to $C\to Y\to S$. Hence $C\to S$ is projective in exactly the convention required in the item.

Let $R_0$ be the integral closure of $R$ in the finite separable extension $L/K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-normal-separable-integral-closure-finite], $R_0$ is finite over $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal], it is a normal domain with fraction field $L$. The ring $R$ is henselian and strictly henselian by hypothesis. Since a domain has only the idempotents $0,1$, [lem-trf-integral-component-henselian-permanence] gives that $R_0$ is local and strictly henselian. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-local-product] it is complete Noetherian local. Finally [lem-sc-integral-closure-dedekind-surjective-fibres] gives that $R_0$ has dimension one, so [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr] makes it a discrete valuation ring. Set $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}R_0$. The inclusion $R\subset R_0$ gives a finite dominant extension of complete strictly henselian traits, with fraction field $k(S_0)=L$.

source.place: More on Algebra Tag 09E8, remark-finite-separable-extension; Tag 092X, lemma-integral-over-henselian; Algebra Tags 032L, 0325, 09IG and 00PD.

proof.text: For each $a\in R_0\subset L\subset F$ and every $c\in C$, a monic equation over $R$ is also a monic equation over the local ring $\mathcal O_{C,c}\subset F$. Because $C$ is normal, $a\in\mathcal O_{C,c}$. Apply [lem-sc-function-field-sections-glue] on $C$: $a$ is a global section. These sections are unique, since sections of the integral $C$ inject into $F$, and addition, multiplication and the $R$-algebra structure agree in $F$. Thus they define an $R$-algebra map $R_0\to\Gamma(C,\mathcal O_C)$. The natural affine-spectrum adjunction [lem-a1-locally-ringed-space-affine-adjunction] yields a morphism $q:C\to S_0$ whose composite with $S_0\to S$ is the structural morphism already constructed. Restricting $q$ along $j$ gives the factorization on $X$ as well. This changes the base of the structural map only: $X$ itself has not been replaced by a fibre product.

source.place: ILO XVI 3.7, printed p.254, first paragraph: extend the trait so its ring is integrally closed in the function field. Local extension of constants uses normality and the sheaf axiom; affine adjunction as in Schemes Tag 01I1.

proof.text: The finite morphism $S_0\to S$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]. Step 5 made the composite $C\xrightarrow qS_0\to S$ H-projective. Apply [lem-per-h-projective-permanence] to this factorization. It gives a closed immersion $C\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_{S_0}$ over $S_0$, so $C$ is projective over $S_0$ without changing its scheme or function field.

source.place: Tag 0C4Q, lemma-projective-permanence, with its finite-projective-space closed-graph proof.

proof.text: The inclusion $R_0\subset F$ is the map on generic stalks of $q$. Every local ring of the integral $C$ is a subring of $F$, so its $R_0$-module is torsion-free: $ab=0$ with $a\ne0$ implies $b=0$ in $F$. A discrete valuation ring is a valuation ring, and [lem-trf-valuation-torsionfree-flat] therefore makes each of these local rings flat over $R_0$. At a point over the closed point of $S_0$ this is precisely flatness over the base local ring $R_0$. At a point over the generic point the base local ring is $L$, and any vector space over a field is flat. Thus $q$ is flat at every point, as required.

Let $C_L$ be the generic fibre of $q$. It is nonempty, integral, and has function field $F$: on affine charts it is obtained by localizing the domains of $C$ at $R_0\setminus\{0\}$. It is finite type over $L$, for the projective embedding in Step 8 gives a finite affine cover by quotients of polynomial $L$-algebras. The field $L$, being algebraic over the characteristic-zero $K$, has characteristic zero, hence is perfect. Apply [lem-kun-geometric-reduced-perfect] to the reduced finite-type $L$-scheme $C_L$; it is geometrically reduced. Also $L$ is algebraically closed in $F$: any element of $F$ algebraic over $L$ is algebraic over $K$ by transitivity of algebraicity and hence lies in $L$ by its definition. By [lem-zl-field-extension-algebraically-closed-geometric], $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is geometrically irreducible over $L$. Then [lem-zl-generic-point-geometric-irreducibility] makes $C_L$ geometrically irreducible. After any field extension it is both reduced and irreducible, hence integral. This proves geometric integrality. Together with Steps 4 and 6 this gives all assertions, including $k(C)=k(X)$ and $k(S_0)=L$ with no extension of $F$.
